messages:
mina: Hi all, first week here — big thanks for the warm welcome! Quick environment puzzle on macOS Ventura (Intel): I'm trying to standardize runtimes with asdf for nodejs/python/ruby, but Homebrew-installed Python and Ruby keep taking precedence. I followed the onboarding doc but: 
- `python3 --version` shows Homebrew Python, not the asdf-managed version
- `gem env` shows GEM_HOME under /usr/local, so `bundle install` puts gems there instead of under the asdf ruby install
Any recommendations for making asdf shims authoritative and avoiding brew clobbering gems/npm globals?
charles: Welcome Mina! Most of this is PATH ordering. Ensure `~/.asdf/shims` and `~/.asdf/bin` are at the front of your PATH. In zsh a safe pattern: 
```
# after sourcing login/profile helpers
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
```
Also reinstall the asdf plugins so they create shims for the versions you expect: `asdf plugin-update --all` and then `asdf reshim`.
lucy: For Ruby specifically, bundler and gem paths can be controlled via `GEM_HOME` and `GEM_PATH`. Our usual setup in dotfiles is: 
```
export GEM_HOME="$HOME/.asdf/installs/ruby/$(asdf current ruby)/lib/ruby/gems/$(ruby -e 'print RUBY_VERSION')"
export PATH="$GEM_HOME/bin:$PATH"
```
That prevents gems from landing in /usr/local.
mina: I'm using zsh with some dotfiles helpers that modify PATH early. I tried adding asdf to the top but `which -a ruby` still shows /usr/local/bin first when I open a fresh terminal. Could macOS login vs interactive ordering be interfering?
charles: Yes. macOS GUI apps launch shells as login shells sometimes; confirm which rc files are being invoked. Put the asdf init in both `~/.zprofile` (login) and `~/.zshrc` (interactive) if needed. Also run `hash -r` after changing PATH to clear zsh's command cache.
ops-bot: Reminder: onboarding checklist item OG-104: "Ensure asdf init in both zprofile and zshrc for macOS".
mina: Good call. One more real-world issue: npm global modules ended up in /usr/local/bin and were shadowing project binstubs. I don't want to mess with system-level /usr/local. What's the clean pattern for npm global installs under asdf node?
sam: We prefer to avoid globals. Use `npx` or add a per-user npm prefix. Example: 
```
mkdir -p ~/.npm-global
npm config set prefix '~/.npm-global'
export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
```
If you're using asdf node, set the prefix to a directory inside the asdf node install for that version (and update PATH) so `npm -g` aligns with the active node. But personally I recommend `corepack` + pnpm or project-local installs.
lucy: Also check Homebrew's shims: on older setups `/usr/local/bin` was earlier in PATH. Homebrew on Apple Silicon uses /opt/homebrew — double-check both. `which -a node` and `echo $PATH` are your friends.
mina: After moving asdf init into `~/.zprofile` and setting npm prefix to `~/.npm-global`, `which -a node` now shows shims first and `npm -g` installs to my home dir. Gems now install to the asdf location after I exported GEM_HOME and reinstalled bundler.
charles: Nice! For VS Code and devcontainers: if you use the 'Open in Container' workflow, update `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` or `devcontainer.json` to set PATH or pass env vars. Host changes don't automatically propagate into containers.
mina: Good to know. Final gotcha: I had created venvs and gemsets before fixing PATH, so they referenced system interpreters. Had to delete and recreate venvs/gemsets.
ops-bot: Created ticket IT-4688: "Update new-hire doc: asdf in zprofile/zshrc, npm prefix guidance, ruby GEM_HOME snippet" assigned to lucy.
mina: Thank you everyone! This cleared up a lot :heart:
